newsitem.title: UK: Champagne flows after British yachtsman rescued.
newsitem.headline: Champagne flows after British yachtsman rescued.

text.p: Relatives of British yachtsman Tony Bullimore celebrated with champagne on Thursday after hearing he had been rescued from the freezing waters between Australia and the Antarctic where he capsized five days ago.
"We opened a bottle of champagne, we're dancing around the room, shouting and screaming, we hug and we kiss," Bullimore's wife Lalel told a radio station.
She was speaking from her home in the southwestern English city of Bristol where she was joined by about 20 other family members.
The British government said it was grateful to the Australian authorities for rescuing Bullimore.
"We are delighted that Mr Bullimore has been found safe and well," said a Foreign Office spokesman.
"We are in close contact with the Australian authorities, via the British Consul General, and we are most grateful to them for bringing about this rescue."
Australian officials said Bullimore, 56, managed to climb free from his upturned yacht after rescuers from a navy frigate knocked on its hull to see if he was still alive.
"HMAS Adelaide put down their rubber inflatable and knocked on the hull," said Mike Calway, a senior official at the Australian Maritime Safety Authority.

"He answered from inside and when they said could he come out, he said 'No, I can't, I can't get out', but next thing he appeared. As far as we are aware he is in reasonable condition," Calway told Reuters.

Bullimore's rescue capped a day of drama in the southern Indian Ocean. Hours earlier, Frenchman Thierry Dubois was winched to safety by a helicopter from the same frigate after drifting for four days in a life raft in heavy seas.
The pair were competing in the Vendee Globe round-the-world yacht race, which has justified its reputation as one of the world's most dangerous sporting events.

Another Frenchman in the same race, Rafael Dinelli, was rescued by the Australian navy on December 26 and a fourth competitor, Canada's Gerry Roufs, was said on Wednesday to have lost radio contact with race organisers.
